subject: SLA template: proposed uptime floor, latency SLOs, and exception scope
messages:
From: Andre Silva <andre.silva@candesce.com>

Cc: contracts@candesce.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template review and a couple of asks on uptime/credits

Hi Olga / Vanessa,

Thanks for sending over the SLA draft. We reviewed the PDF (attached) and have a few high-level items we need to align on before legal will proceed:

- Uptime floor: our infosec & platform teams prefer a 99.95% monthly uptime for production (we're willing to accept 99.9% for non-prod). Can Redwood confirm the default offered level and whether it can be tiered by environment?
- Monthly credit cap: we typically see a cap expressed as a percentage of monthly spend (e.g., up to X%) — would Redwood be willing to do a capped percentage rather than a flat dollar cap?
- Planned maintenance carveout: time-zone coordination may require more than 4 hours/month in our case. Can we discuss expanding the scheduled maintenance carveout?
- Latency SLOs: we need a clear statement of how you measure generation latency (p95 or p99?) and whether large-batch background jobs can affect the SLA measurement windows.

Attached: Redwood_SLA_Template_v1.pdf (redlined). Please advise next steps and a short timeline — we are trying to get final terms into our procurement queue this month.

Thanks,
Andre Silva
VP Platform Engineering
Candesce Health

--

Subject: Re: SLA template review and a couple of asks on uptime/credits

Andre —

Appreciate the clear notes and the redlines. Quick answers up front, then detail below:

- Default uptime: Redwood's hosted offering is typically 99.95% for production workloads and 99.9% for non-production. We can reflect both levels in the template and let you pick per-environment at signing.
- Credit cap: we can offer a percentage-based cap; our usual is a monthly maximum equal to 15% of the monthly invoice for hosted customers. For Dedicated customers we negotiate a different cap tied to committed spend.
- Planned maintenance: our standard carveout is up to 4 hours/month; we can discuss increasing to 8 hours/month for customers with global maintenance windows, provided maintenance windows are scheduled with 5 business days' notice and limited to quarterly larger migrations.
- Latency SLO measurement: we measure generation latency at the request level across the customer's production model routes. Our baseline is p95 < 200ms for single-request, synchronous text-generation (tokenization to final chunk). For conversational flows with function/tool calls or very long-context, SLO narrative will call out an adjusted leniency. We exclude background batch scoring jobs from the SLA window unless those requests are routed through the same production endpoints and impact p95 for traffic in that window.

Concretely, here's a proposal we can insert into the template (we'll put this in the PDF and CSV credit table):
- UPTIME BAND -> CREDIT
  - >= 99.95% -> 0% credit
  - 99.9% - 99.949% -> 10% of monthly invoice
  - 99.0% - 99.899% -> 40% of monthly invoice
  - < 99.0% -> 100% of monthly invoice (or termination right after 30 days of persistent <99.0%)
- Monthly credit cap: 15% of monthly invoice (hosted).
- Planned maintenance carveout: up to 4 hours/month by default; up to 8 hours/month with mutual agreement and scheduled maintenance windows (5-business-days notice).
- Measurement window: monthly, UTC calendar month; downtime counted as minutes where route-level availability falls below defined thresholds.

I'll loop Marcus to get legal-level language tightened on definitions for "downtime" and for carveouts tied to customer config. Vanessa — can you confirm we have a single canonical measurement method in the Console (token counts, timestamps) and a short export we can point to for audit?

If that sounds close to what you need, I'll update the PDF and send a clean draft for your procurement team.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Andre / team —

Thanks, Olga — this is a good starting point. A few legal/contract items we should tighten before we send the final:

1) Definition of "Downtime" — propose we explicitly define as "route-level unavailability where HTTP 5xx or no-response is returned for more than X consecutive seconds for production-rate traffic," and exclude transient client-side failures.
2) Measurement methodology — add an appendix that explains sampling and aggregation (p95 latency measured over production requests excluding canary/diagnostic traffic). It'll help procurement to see the export.
3) Credit cap: 15% monthly cap is acceptable for hosted. For customers on reserved/dedicated capacity we will put a negotiated cap based on committed spend (to be added to a schedule).
4) Excessive maintenance exception — propose that any maintenance longer than 72 continuous hours that causes unavailability triggers a one-time escalation process rather than an automatic credit, to give us time to remediate high-impact migrations.

I attached a simple CSV showing how credits map to monthly invoices (SLA_credit_table.csv). Please review and tell me if you want different percentage breakpoints or different language on termination rights.

Marcus Lin
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Olga / Marcus —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A couple of final asks so we can move to procurement sign-off:

- Planned maintenance carveout: we can accept the 4-hour default, but can you make the 8-hour option explicit as a negotiated term (we'd like the option due to our global traffic patterns)? If you can put the 8-hour path into the template as an alternate box to check, that would be ideal.
- Latency SLO: for synchronous inference endpoints we'd prefer p99 rather than p95 given downstream SLAs; will Redwood accept p99 for that class of endpoints?
- Measurement exports: can Redwood include a one-click export from the Console that shows route-level uptime and p99/p95 latency for the prior 3 months? If so, please state that clearly in the template as the authoritative measurement report.

If you can confirm these three items in a clean PDF we can circulate internally and get the PO raised. Appreciate the pragmatic approach — looking forward to the updated doc.

Regards,
Andre Silva
VP Platform Engineering
Candesce Health
